claims.text: The AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is cobalt-free.
Adding an in-situ laser re-melting pass after each powder-bed-fusion layer will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
The re-melting pass will promote atomic diffusion.
The re-melting pass will reduce compositional segregation.
The re-melting pass will reduce residual stress.
Conventionally processed powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi exhibits segregation, residual thermal stress, and associated defects.
A suitably optimized laser energy input can completely re-melt each layer without overheating it.
The proposed process uses an inert atmosphere and small parts with dimensions below approximately 100 mm.
Laser re-melting will produce a more compositionally homogeneous microstructure.
Laser re-melting will produce a finer and more uniform grain structure.
The additional laser pass creates a transient fully liquid state in each layer.
Enhanced atomic diffusion in the transient liquid state homogenizes the elemental distribution.
The re-melting process relaxes thermal gradients and thereby diminishes residual stress.
The re-melting process mitigates defect formation during subsequent solidification.
Re-melted samples will have greater yield strength than samples produced by powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
Re-melted samples will have greater ductility than samples produced by powder-bed fusion without re-melting.
Powder-bed-fused AlCrFeNiSi without re-melting has higher segregation, residual stress, and defect density than the proposed re-melted material.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to small-scale builds made under a controlled inert atmosphere.
Applicability to larger parts or substantially different process parameters is not established.
